steps: A chloroplast is a green plastid found in plant cells, especially in the cells of leaves.
It is surrounded by a double membrane.
Its interior contains a fluid called stroma and flattened membrane sacs called thylakoids; stacks of thylakoids are called grana.
Chlorophyll is present in the thylakoid membranes and absorbs light energy.
Chloroplasts are the sites of photosynthesis, in which light energy is used to make food (glucose) from carbon dioxide and water; oxygen is released.
items.finalAnswer: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis to make food for the plant.

steps: Water enters a plant cell by osmosis through its selectively permeable cell membrane.
The water collects in the vacuole, causing it to swell.
The swollen vacuole and cytoplasm push against the cell wall.
The pressure exerted by the cell contents against the cell wall is called turgor pressure.
The cell wall resists this pressure, helping the cell remain firm.
items.finalAnswer: Turgor pressure develops when water enters a plant cell by osmosis and the swollen cell contents press against the cell wall.

steps: Plant cells have a cell wall; animal cells do not.
Plant cells usually have chloroplasts; animal cells do not.
Plant cells usually have one large central vacuole; animal cells have small vacuoles or none.
Plant cells usually have a fixed, regular shape; animal cells usually have an irregular or rounded shape.
items.finalAnswer: Plant and animal cells differ in the presence of a cell wall and chloroplasts, the size of their vacuoles, and their usual shape.

steps: Division of labour is the sharing of different jobs among different parts of an organism.
In multicellular organisms, cells become specialized to perform particular functions efficiently.
Similar specialized cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs work together in organ systems.
Red blood cells transport oxygen around the body.
Nerve cells carry nerve impulses.
Muscle cells contract to produce movement.
items.finalAnswer: Division of labour means that specialized cells, tissues, organs and organ systems perform different functions in a multicellular organism.

steps: Cell specialization is the process by which a cell develops a particular structure to perform a particular function.
Specialized cells perform their functions more efficiently.
For example, a red blood cell is specialized to transport oxygen, while a nerve cell is specialized to carry nerve impulses.
In multicellular organisms, specialized cells work together to perform the activities needed by the organism.
items.finalAnswer: Cell specialization is the development of structures that enable cells to perform particular functions efficiently.

steps: Mitochondria release energy from food during cellular respiration.
If mitochondria become dysfunctional or are absent, the cell cannot obtain enough energy for its activities.
Organelles that need energy to perform their functions may then work slowly or may stop working.
This can affect important processes such as the synthesis and transport of materials and the maintenance of the cell.
items.finalAnswer: Mitochondrial dysfunction or absence reduces the cell’s energy supply, impairing the activities of other organelles.

steps: The nucleus contains DNA, which carries the instructions for making proteins.
The nucleus provides instructions, and ribosomes use these instructions to make proteins.
If coordination between the nucleus and ribosomes fails, the correct proteins may not be made.
Without the required proteins, cell structures and processes may not function properly.
This coordination is important because proteins are needed for the growth, repair and normal functioning of the cell.
items.finalAnswer: Coordination between the nucleus and ribosomes is essential for making the proteins required for normal cell functioning.
